$comment: The checks that must be green before anything lands on master — enumerated here so
the answer to 'what would actually stop this change?' lives in the repository rather
than in one person's GitHub settings page.
This file is not decorative. `npm run merge-gate` (inside `npm run check:ci`, which
CI runs and .husky/pre-push runs before every push to master) reads it and fails when
a named check no longer exists, no longer runs on pull requests, has been renamed, or
has been softened with `continue-on-error` on a step that is not listed in
`softenedSteps`. So a check cannot quietly stop being a gate.
`check` is the string GitHub shows as the status check — the job's `name:`. It is what
you type into Settings → Branches → require status checks. Keep the two in step: this
file is the source, the settings page is the copy.
A required status check only bites on a pull request, and this repo lands most changes by
direct push to master. So every check here also has a local leg inside `npm run check:ci`,
which .husky/pre-push runs before any push that updates master — including the rubric
review, which reaches check:ci as `npm run review:agent:gate`. That is what makes 'this
would have stopped the change' true on the path changes actually take, rather than only on
the path a contributor takes. test-unit/delivery-contract.test.mjs asserts the wiring.
Rung discipline (docs/adr/0007-gate-rung-discipline.md) decides what belongs here: a
check is required only if it passes today. The reporting-rung jobs — sast.yml's
`semgrep`, supply-chain.yml's `audit`, agent-review.yml's `judgment`, and
agent-review-history.yml's `history` and `publish` — are deliberately absent, and
each one's workflow says why. Promoting one means fixing its findings, dropping its
`continue-on-error`, and adding it here in the same commit. sast.yml's `repo-rules`
was promoted that way on 2026-09-01: four findings closed, the softening line deleted,
and `npm run sast` added to check:ci so the push path is covered too.
The `check` string below is also read back by scripts/agent-review-history.mjs, which
uses it to find the blocking job's annotations when it aggregates what the review has
caught. That is deliberate: one declaration of the name, and a rename that forgets this
file fails the merge gate before it can make the report aggregate nothing.

required.why: `npm run check:ci` — the single command that reproduces the gate locally. Typecheck is also the i18n parity check, so a locale column added on one side only dies here.
The only layer that loads a whole page. Hydration errors, broken anchors and demo-mode fallbacks are invisible to tsc, the unit suite and `next build`.

Part A of .github/agent-review-rubric.md. ~97% of commits here are written by an agent and triaged weekly; these six rules are the ways a green build can be bought rather than earned — or, for A5, the way the log stops being bisectable — so the review has to be able to stop a merge and not merely comment on one.

Token scope, no privileged trigger (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment — each one starts a job in the base repo's context on an outsider's event), no moving-branch action refs, third-party actions pinned, container images digest-pinned, and no attacker-controlled context outside an `env:` binding — not in a `run:` script, not in a `with:` input, not in an `if:`. This repository's secrets are advertiser OAuth tokens.

The ten rules in scripts/sast.mjs encode what an off-the-shelf pack cannot see here: every route under src/app/api establishes caller identity (ADR-0002 — an unverified projectId does not 401, it mints an empty tenant that reads as 'no data yet'), no "use client" module reads a server env var, no route imports the decrypted BYOM key, no SQL is built by interpolation, nothing credential-shaped reaches console. ~97% of commits here are agent-written and the process holds live Google Ads, Sklik and Resend credentials, so a security finding has to be able to stop a change rather than annotate one.
A leaked credential is not a 'report it later' class of problem, and the pre-commit hook only ever sees the commit in front of it.
